text:
dmitri: quick follow-up from the offload RFC — I'm sketching a small refactor: introduce a "prefetch contract" between the eviction coordinator and the slab allocator. goal: make prefetch intents first-class so we can reason about credits and failures separately from allocation paths.

maggie: curious — what's the new surface? basically more args on alloc() or a new API?

dmitri: new API. rough idea: Evictor -> Allocator: request_prefetch(id, page_range, priority) -> returns prefetch_token or error. Allocator uses token to do async staging and attach metadata to pages. if token expires or fails, Allocator signals back.

kevin: can you paste a minimal signature?

dmitri: sure:
```
// evictor -> allocator
prefetch_token_t request_prefetch(range_t r, prefetch_priority p, deadline d)
// allocator -> evictor (async)
void prefetch_ack(prefetch_token_t t, status_t s, resident_meta m)
```

anya: my first question — why not piggyback prefetch on existing alloc()/get() flows? more APIs = more surface area.

dmitri: good point. tradeoff: piggybacking keeps surface minimal but mixes failure modes (allocation OOM vs prefetch miss). explicit tokens let us: 1) rate-limit/credit prefetches separately, 2) provide telemetry when prefetches miss, 3) allow eviction to cancel outstanding prefetches easily.

liz: also helps when we want to expose prefetch telemetry to Optimize. separate contract = clearer SLO signals.

kevin: what's the expected latency impact on the hot path? we can't add sync handshakes.

dmitri: prefetch is async. hot path still uses existing fast-path alloc/get. Prefetch token handling only affects background staging and future requests. worst-case: token overhead on evictor path is a small enqueue + sequence number.

maggie: eviction ordering question: if a prefetch is outstanding for a page that later becomes a candidate for evict, who wins?

dmitri: allocator maintains a token->page mapping. evictor can query token state: cancel_token(t) or wait_for_token(t) with timeout. cancel is preferred; if prefetch completes before cancel, we keep resident. if cancel wins, prefetch result is discarded.

anya: how do we do credit accounting across tenants? today we have tenant quotas for allocation. prefetches could blow up network / staging bandwidth.

dmitri: plan: separate credit pool for prefetch that counts against tenant bandwidth budget but with different burst/steady rules. also ability to throttle globally when staging node is saturated.

kevin: sounds complex. can we iterate? land a minimal version that only creates tokens and has a no-op cancel path, then expand credits later.

dmitri: yes — roadmap in patches:
- v1 (poC): request_prefetch/token lifecycle, cancel, no accounting, metrics only
- v2: add credits + tenant policies, throttling hooks
- v3: integrate with CompactSlab refactor: allow slab to migrate prefetched pages into compact arenas

liz: for v1 let's define telemetry fields: prefetch_requested, prefetch_completed, prefetch_cancelled, prefetch_latency_ms, prefetch_hit_on_next_request. Optimize needs the last one.

maggie: tests? we need unit tests for token lifecycle and an integration perf job to prove no regression on 95th latency.

dmitri: agreed. I'll add unit tests + a canary workload: small seq-length model with aggressive eviction to force prefetch churn.

anya: rollout plan? feature flag gated? telemetry dashboard?

dmitri: feature flag `allocator_prefetch_v1` default off. rollout to staging -> canary hosts -> 10% prod -> 100%. dashboard: a new panel under "runtime/prefetch" with the telemetry Liz listed.

kevin: one more thing: how does this interact with continuous batching? if a batch holds KV cache that depends on in-flight prefetches, cancellations might freeze a batch. we need clear contract: batches only consult resident_meta; if not resident they either trigger sync load or backfill from fallback.

dmitri: yep will document: prefetch is hint-only. it can improve latency for subsequent requests but batches must be resilient: do fallback sync-fetch if resident_meta absent.

liz: can you add a short note about safety: prefetch tokens must be idempotent and survive coordinator retries. also ensure token caps per-evictor to avoid leak when allocator restarts.

dmitri: noted. token -> opaque id with sequence + evictor id; allocator persists transient state in in-memory index and exposes reconciliation API on startup.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: update allocator proto, add feature flag, add telemetry schema, add cancel rpc, add unit/integration tests.

kevin: ok seems reasonable. next actions: Dmitri to open a draft RFC/PR with the API + unit tests; Maggie to own perf job; Liz to spec telemetry panels; Anya to review the proto for minimalism.

anya: ack, will review proto once PR is up.

maggie: I'll sketch the perf harness tomorrow. :thumbsup:

dmitri: thanks all — I'll post the PR link here when ready. :rocket:
